title: Harness
explainer: How agents are set up to work in this repository
sentence: This repository speaks to agents through {documents, plural, one {# document} other {# documents}} and has {checks, plural, one {# check} other {# checks}} in place.
checksBreakdown: {hooks, plural, one {# hook script} other {# hook scripts}} · {gitHooks, plural, one {# file under .githooks/} other {# files under .githooks/}} · {scripts, plural, one {# package.json script} other {# package.json scripts}}
checksHint: "Checks" counts declarations, not distinct guards: a hook mirrored for Claude Code and for Codex is two scripts for one guard, .githooks/ holds helper modules beside its hooks, and the script list includes watch mode and the lanes a single run re-runs. What it counts is hook scripts a config names that exist on disk, files under .githooks/, and package.json lint, typecheck and test scripts. Whether any of them runs, or has ever caught anything, is not something we can know from files.
guidesTitle: Guides: what the agents were told
guidesCaption: Documents an agent reads before it starts work. Each tool reads a different set.
columnChangedHint: When the file was last modified on this disk. Not a commit date: a fresh copy stamps every file with the time it arrived.
toolsUncitedHint: Which tool reads which file comes from that tool's documentation, not from this repository. This row has no document behind it.
capMerged: Codex reads the root AGENTS.md merged with the nested AGENTS.md on the working path, and silently truncates the merge past the cap. The bar measures the merged length.
pairCompared: {count, plural, one {# reference pair compared} other {# reference pairs compared}}
pairHint: Compares same-named Codex and Claude guidance for reference. Tool-specific instructions may differ; a content difference is not an error or a requirement to synchronize them.
driftTitle: {count, plural, one {# content difference} other {# content differences}}
driftOnlyIn: Only in {dir}; the twin folder has no copy.
pairFilesMissing: {count, plural, one {# file missing} other {# files missing}}
pairFilesNoTwin: {count, plural, one {# file has no twin} other {# files have no twin}}
driftLineMark: Matching lines share a row; a line with no match is marked +.
driftSideMarked: {count, plural, one {# line with no match in the {other} file} other {# lines with no match in the {other} file}}
driftSideLacks: {count, plural, one {# line the {other} file lacks} other {# lines the {other} file lacks}}
driftLineMarkUnaligned: These files are too long to align line by line; a line only one of the Claude Code and Codex files has is highlighted.
driftInvisibleOnly: The visible text is the same; only line endings, trailing spaces or the final newline differ.
hooksCaption: Not a rule in prose: code that actually blocks or records.
hookWiredHint: The script the config names exists on disk. Whether it runs is not something we can know from files.
hookMissingHint: The config names this path and the file is not there. That produces no error and no block: the guard you counted on is silently absent.
hookUnresolvedHint: The command is not a script path, so we could not ask whether a file exists.
hookApprovalGateHint: Codex hashes every hook entry and will not run a new or changed one until a person trusts it in /hooks. That approval lives in no file, so we cannot read it.
browserOnlyBody: Most harness files live in dot directories: .claude, .agents, .codex. A browser's folder permission cannot see those entries at all, so a list drawn here would show far fewer files than exist. The desktop app reads all of them.
noSourceBody: The harness belongs to the repository agents actually edit. Connect a source folder to a project and this list fills in. When more than one folder is connected we do not pick which harness you meant.
failedNotGranted: Atlas reads a connected code folder only when it is the repository holding the folder you opened, or a folder you chose in this app since it last opened. {path} is neither, so none of its files were read and nothing is counted here.
failedMissing: {path} is not there any more, so none of its files were read and nothing is counted here.
failedUnsupported: This version of the app reads a connected code folder's harness files on macOS only, so none of {path}'s files were read and nothing is counted here.
failedBody: Part of {path} could not be read, so nothing is counted here until it can be.
emptyBody: There is no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules here. Agents start on this repository having been told nothing about it.
coverageTableCaption: Domains of this repository, and what tells, gates and watches each one.
coverageColumnToldHint: Guides whose declared path reaches a path the ontology records for this domain: a nested AGENTS.md for its folder, a .claude rule whose paths: match, or a hook that adds context when a session starts or a prompt is sent and whose script names those paths. A file is here because its declared path reaches the domain, never because a tool probably reads it.
coverageColumnGatedHint: Hook scripts that run just before a tool call, and files under .githooks/, whose text names this domain's paths. The script exists; whether it has ever stopped anything is not in the files.
coverageColumnWatchedHint: Hooks that run after a tool call or at other events, package.json lint, typecheck and test scripts, and CI jobs whose paths: filter names this domain's paths; paths-ignore is not a path. A check that has never failed cannot tell safe code from a blind check.
coverageRule: A file appears in a domain when a path it declares reaches a path the ontology records for that domain. Open a cell to see the declaration it came from.
coverageUnreached: {count, plural, one {# recorded path is} other {# recorded paths are}} reached by no path-scoped guide: {paths}. The always-loaded rules still reach them.
coverageOutside: {count, plural, one {# check or gate names} other {# checks and gates name}} a folder the ontology records no path in: {folders}.
coveragePathless: {count, plural, one {# capability records} other {# capabilities record}} no implementation path, so nothing here can reach it.
coverageNoAreasTitle: This repository has agent files and no ontology yet
coverageNoAreasBody: The matrix puts this repository's own domains on its rows, and those come from the ontology: a domain a person defined, with the implementation path each of its capabilities points at. Without them there is nothing to be told, gated or watched about. {documents, plural, one {# guide document was} other {# guide documents were}} still found, and the Guides view lists every one. Define a domain with a capability that carries a path, and the rows appear.
coverageOpenNames: {column} for {area}: {count, plural, =0 {nothing names this domain} one {# declaration} other {# declarations}}
coverageEverywhereBody: Declares no path, so it applies everywhere. Listed once here instead of in all {areas} rows. It is also why an empty cell above reads “nothing names this domain” rather than “nothing runs over it”.
coverageDiscoveredTests: {count, plural, =0 {No test file sits under its recorded paths either.} one {# test file sits under its recorded paths and runs under the repository-wide lanes.} other {# test files sit under its recorded paths and run under the repository-wide lanes.}}
loadingDetail: Reads only agent guides, hooks and check files; nothing else is opened.
anatomySilentGuards: {count, plural, one {# script this config names is not on disk} other {# scripts these configs name are not on disk}}: {scripts}. That produces no block and no error; the guard is simply absent.
overviewNoGaps: No gaps: each of the {domains, plural, one {# domain} other {# domains}} with a recorded path has a file in all three columns.
overviewHandoff: Copy the request for your agent
overviewHandoffCopied: Copied. Paste it into your coding agent's chat in this repository.
overviewHandoffCopyFailed: Could not copy. Open "See the request" and copy the text by hand.
overviewCellHint: Press a cell to open the files that make it.
overviewNoPathBody: No capability in this domain records an implementation path, so no file can name it. It is not counted as a gap.
overviewEverywhereApplies: Also applies here: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} that reach every domain.
overviewPermissions: {count, plural, one {# deny or ask rule} other {# deny or ask rules}} in {config}
overviewLoopNote: Which model runs, what it reads first and when it stops belong to the agent tool, so files cannot show them.
coverageColumnGatedGloss: Hooks that filter before a tool runs
overviewEverywhereGloss: Root guides, permission rules and hooks that name no path
overviewVerdictOne: <name>{domain}</name> · {column}: no file directly names this domain’s paths. What reaches every domain still applies.
overviewVerdictMany: <name>{domain}</name> · {column} and {rest} more {rest, plural, one {cell have} other {cells have}} no file directly naming their domain’s paths. What reaches every domain still applies to them.
overviewVerdictCaption: The request goes to your clipboard only · Atlas sends nothing
overviewPanelEmpty: Pick a cell and the files that make it open here
overviewFillsHeadingGap: Files that could fill this cell
